⚡ The price cap rose 13% on 1 July. The typical household now pays £1,862 a year — £221 more — and 5.5 million homes will now spend a fifth of their income on energy.

Ministers blame the Strait of Hormuz. But Britain chose dependence on imported gas — squeezing the North Sea, delaying nuclear, stacking levies on bills. When a strait closes on the other side of the world and your bill jumps £221, that's policy, not weather.
